text:
ashley: NA3 GPU pools: sharp p95 jump on text-gen starting ~04:18Z, users hitting 400-600ms extra per request. Queues building, evictions up. spotted right after runtime canary. any eyeballs?
priya: looking — can you paste the top lines from the batcher metric and a few lines of the runtime logs?
ashley: paste: ```batcher.pending_requests=124
batcher.max_batch_size=96
batcher.avg_wait_ms=37.8
kv_cache.evictions=312/min
runtime: continuous-batcher v2.4.0 commit f3a2e: set default max_wait_ms=20 previously 5```
miguel: that avg_wait_ms and the max_wait change smell like the recent continuous-batcher tweak. if max_wait_ms increased to 20 we can get larger batches at the cost of tail latency. NA3 traffic pattern has many short requests so larger batch aggregation hurts p95.
ben: deploy-bot shows canary rollout id 2026-02-29_0420 -> nodes in na3 got it. rollback option available.
deploy-bot: canary 2026-02-29_0420 started by @maria at 04:19Z, 12/50 shards applied. current status: applied_to=12, progress=24%
ashley: priority: we need to both stop tail latencies and avoid wholesale outage. ideas: 1) force small-batch mode via runtime flag, 2) divert some traffic to dedicated pools, 3) rollback canary. tradeoffs?
priya: small-batch flag is fastest low-risk (just flips config). rolling back canary affects availability but is effective. diverting to dedicated increases cost and may hit reserved capacity.
miguel: canary only on some shards — rollback will take ~7m to finish and drop latency but has flapping risk. small-batch flag (max_batch=8, max_wait_ms=5) can be pushed via remote-config and takes effect almost immediately. recommend flag first.
ben: pushing remote-config now: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG' https://config.redwood/api/flags -d '{"continuous_batch.small_batch":true, "max_batch_size":8, "max_wait_ms":5}'`
ashley: executing. will report metrics.
(30s later) ashley: ran flag push, restarting batcher processes on the 12 canary shards via `infra restart batcher --shard 1024-1036`
cloud-status-bot: note — minor network route flap reported in provider NA3-egress at 04:21Z, AS path churn. impacting packet loss ~0.2% for 10m.
priya: good callout — network flap might amplify latency. keep watch.
miguel: metrics: `p95_gen_latency` before=980ms, after_flag=430ms, after_restarts=210ms. queue depth dropping from 120 -> 8. kv_cache.evictions down to 18/min.
ashley: routing note: shifted 8% of low-priority traffic to dedicated pools as a safety valve using tag: `evac=lowprio` (policy run at 04:26Z). cost hit small for now.
ben: added temporary rate-limit on free-tier routes to 20r/s to reduce pressure. open ticket to reconcile bill impact for today.
priya: monitoring dashboards look stable. plan: keep small-batch flag for 30m, then evaluate canary rollback vs flag permanence. if everything stable, we'll stop diverting traffic and remove rate limits.
miguel: log followup: capture container logs for one shard to /var/logs/incident/1719991234.log and attach to postmortem.
ashley: ack. creating incident record and starting timeline. thanks all. :thumbsup:
(10m later) ashley: p95 holding ~210ms for 8m straight, queue depth <15. leaving this thread open for 30m then closing if stable.
